q: Optics is the branch of physics that studies the nature and properties of light.
e: True. A different driver in place of Optics would describe a different law. Optics and branch have to stay with the same process.

q: A laser, acronym for Light Amplification by Spontaneous Emission of Radiation, is a source of a narrow beam of intense, monochromatic, coherent light.
e: False. Laser is Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation, not spontaneous. Spontaneous emission is random in phase and direction. Stimulated emission copies the stimulating photon.

q: A laser produces stimulated emission of photons from excited atoms or molecules.
e: True. The beam is coherent, monochromatic, narrow and intense. Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and stimulated emission; the cavity is two mirrors.

q: Lasers are classified into three main types: gas lasers, solid-state lasers, and fiber lasers.
e: False. The usual three-way split is gas, solid-state, and semiconductor lasers. Fibre lasers are a solid-state family, not a third top-level class in this listing. Pumping and the medium are what define the type.

q: A laser contains three essential elements: laser medium, power supply and optical cavity.
e: True. Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and a mirror cavity; the beam is coherent and monochromatic. Spontaneous emission is random in phase and is not the laser process.

q: The laser medium is the material emitting the laser beam.
e: True. Spontaneous emission is random in phase and is not the laser process. Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and a mirror cavity; the beam is coherent and monochromatic.

q: The power supply delivers energy to the laser medium in the form needed to excite it to emit light, a process called focusing.
e: False. Delivering energy to the laser medium so it can emit is pumping, not focusing. Focusing is what lenses do to a beam. Population inversion comes from that pump.

q: The optical cavity concentrates the light to stimulate the emission of laser radiation.
e: True. It travels at the speed of light. Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and a mirror cavity; the beam is coherent and monochromatic.

q: The optical cavity consists of two highly refractive lenses.
e: False. A laser cavity is two mirrors, one of them partly transmitting, not two highly refractive lenses. The mirrors send the light back through the medium. Lenses may sit outside; they are not the cavity.

q: Two essential processes to initiate a laser action are spontaneous emission and population inversion.
e: False. The two essentials for laser action are stimulated emission and population inversion. Spontaneous emission starts stray photons, but the amplification is stimulated. Random spontaneous light is not the beam.

q: In stimulated emission, the transition occurs when the atom in its excited state interacts with an incident photon at the transition frequency.
e: True. Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and stimulated emission; the cavity is two mirrors. The beam is coherent, monochromatic, narrow and intense.

q: Atoms undergoing stimulated emission radiate photons of different frequencies in random directions and out of phase with the stimulating radiation.
e: False. Stimulated emission radiates photons of the same frequency, in the same direction, and in phase with the stimulating wave. Random frequencies and phases are spontaneous emission. Coherence is the laser signature.

q: For stimulated emission to occur, a population inversion would be needed.
e: True. Laser means light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Laser action needs population inversion and stimulated emission; the cavity is two mirrors. Stimulated emission to occur a population inversion cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: Population inversion means the population of the upper level of a transition would have to be higher than that of the lower level.
e: True. Population and inversion have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of Population would describe a different law.

q: One of the unique properties of a laser beam is incoherence, which means that the light waves it contains are out of phase with one another.
e: False. A laser beam is coherent: the waves stay in phase. Incoherence is ordinary lamp light. Monochromaticity and a narrow beam ride with that coherence.

q: A typical beam divergence is around a milliradian.
e: True. A different driver in place of typical would describe a different law. typical and beam have to stay with the same process.

q: Lasers are used in optical fibre communications to send information over large distances.
e: True. An optical fibre guides light in a core by total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary. Incidence must exceed the critical angle or light leaks. Information rides as light pulses, not as copper electrical pulses.

q: Laser range finders are used to determine the chemical composition of an object.
e: False. Laser range finders measure distance from go-and-return time. Chemical composition is spectroscopy, often with a different laser setup. Timing a pulse is not a composition assay.
